title: Forkstream payments — partner engagement dossier
content:
One-pager brain dump + outreach plan for Forkstream (payments platform for SMB retail chains)

Quick background (what I pulled together)
- Forkstream is a mid-stage fintech (Series B-ish from Crunchbase) focused on card processing + value-add services for multi-location retailers.
- Recent hires in product and integrations (LinkedIn: Head of Integrations = R. Morales) — signals they want tighter partner ecosystem.
- Pricing: interchange-plus model with monthly minimums. Public docs limited; partner pages mention add-on APIs for refunds, disputes, and webhook event streams.
- Compliance: PCI SAQ requirements, they host tokenization service (see product screenshots in deck).
- Tech stack clues: API-first, webhooks, Postgres, Ruby backends (per job posts).

Why Redwood might fit / value props to surface
- Lower per-request latency for on-device POS assistants compared with them routing to back-end LLMs; reduce token spend for templated responses (caching + prefix reuse).
- Private deployment option for regulated merchants (big chains) — strong signal for Forkstream enterprise deals.
- Cost predictability for them: Dedicated/Dedicated-reserve could be sold as a white-labeled partner inference endpoint for merchant-facing chat/receipt summarization features.
- Observability/rollouts: helpful for controlled pilot (canary across stores/regions).

Target use-cases to propose (initial pilot ideas)
1) POS assistant for cashiers — fast answers about returns, SKU substitutions, basic troubleshooting. Needs sub-200ms local latency target for UX.
2) Automated dispute summarization — ingest chargeback docs and produce a succinct summary + recommended evidence pack for merchants.
3) Receipt summarization & search (embeddings) — compressed store-level vector index for retrieving past receipts, promotions, and loyalty matches.
4) Smart routing fallback: high-confidence answers served by smaller quantized local model; fall back to larger model for complex queries.

Key technical asks we would need from them (pre-pilot)
- Expected QPS profile (peak/day, distribution by store).
- Typical prompt lengths (receipt size, chat context lengths).
- PCI compliance boundary and whether sending PII or card data to third-party inference endpoints is allowed (probably not).
- Whether they can host Redwood Private in their VPC (preferred) or need dedicated managed hosting.
- What telemetry they can expose for P0 metrics (latency, error traces, token counts).

Outreach cadence draft (sequence for initial contact)
- Day 0: Intro email to Head of Integrations (R. Morales) and Head of Product — subject: "Pilot idea: on-device POS assistant + dispute summarization (low lift)". Short 4-line pitch + 1-sentence ask for 20-min exploratory.
- Day 3: LinkedIn connect + note referencing a specific Forkstream job or blog post (personalized).
- Day 7: Follow-up with a 2-slide PDF (pilot sketch + metrics we can aim for: <200ms median latency, 40% reduction in dispute triage hours).
- Day 14: Call attempt; if no response, send a customer use-case case study (anonymized SMB chain where we cut token costs by ~35%) and ask for intro to integrations lead if wrong person.

Sample short email (cold) — keep punchy
Subject: Pilot: faster POS assistant + dispute summaries for Forkstream\nHi R. — I’m Aisha on the partnerships team at Redwood Inference. We help payments platforms run LLM features (POS assistants, dispute summarization, receipt search) with predictable latency/cost and deployment options that meet PCI constraints.

Quick idea: 6–8 week pilot to run a POS assistant on a dedicated endpoint (or in Forkstream VPC) with metrics: median latency <200ms, token cost down 30% via prefix caching and small-model routing.

If interested, 20 min next week to validate feasibility?
Aisha

Call script bullets (first intro call)
- 3 min: company intros + what I’d like to learn (current pain, timelines, pilot owners).
- 5 min: product fit examples + demo pointers (we can screen-share low-fi latency metrics and embedding retrieval demo).
- 7 min: Ops details: PCI boundaries, where models can run (hosted/dedicated/private), SSO/KMS needs.
- 3 min: Next steps + propose pilot charter (metrics + stakeholders).

Common objections & quick rebuttals
- "We can do this with our internal ML team"
  - Rebuttal: likely true for a long-term build, but we can do a time-boxed pilot that proves UX and unit economics in 6–8 weeks; we integrate with your telemetry and hand over artifacts for internal adoption.
- "PCI and data privacy concerns — can't send cardholder data"
  - Rebuttal: we can run Redwood Private in customer VPC or on-prem, and tokenization can be performed prior to any model call. We also have enterprise contracts and audit logs.
- "Token cost / pricing uncertainty"
  - Rebuttal: offer a fixed trial pricing for pilot + compute estimate for projected QPS; show historical pilot that reduced token spend via caching and rerouting.
- "Latency concerns for cashier UX"
  - Rebuttal: can target <200ms median via dedicated endpoints, local quantized variants + dynamic batching tuned to POS patterns. We’ll prototype with subset of stores first.

Success metrics for pilot (measurable)
- Median inference latency (goal <200ms).
- Token spend per interaction (goal reduce 25–40% vs naive calls).
- CSR / cashier time saved for dispute triage (hours/week).
- Accuracy /Quality guardrails: % of answers flagged as needing human review (target <10%).

Risks & unknowns (open questions)
- Will Forkstream accept running partner code in their VPC or insist on managed hosted model?
- Are there legal constraints in their terms with merchants preventing third-party inference?
- Can we get sample event streams and non-sensitive receipt data for model tuning?
- Integration ownership — do they want Redwood to implement the POS hooks or will they own engineering?

Quick technical sketch for internal ENG review (notes to Marcus)
- Minimal pilot footprint: 1 dedicated GPU endpoint (g5/4 equivalent) + ephemeral batch worker for offline embedding index builds.
- Inference config: small quantized LLM for intent classification + mid-sized opt for generation. Prefix cache for common Q/A (returns policy, SKUs).
- Webhook flow: Forkstream events -> Redwood ingress (or VPC peering) -> routing layer -> model -> response back to POS via webhook.
- Logging: token counts, per-route latency, response size; set up alerts on tail latency > 500ms.

Next actions (short list)
- Finalize 1-page pilot sketch (2 slides) and attach to first outbound. (Aisha)
- Reach out to R. Morales + product lead with short email this week. (Aisha)
- Sync with Marcus on rough cost estimate and recommended infra profile. (Marcus)
- Create sandbox dataset request template for non-PII receipt samples. (Lina)

Notes-to-self / reminders
- Personalize outbound with quote from their latest engineering blog or a specific job posting to increase open rate.
- If they push for references, use anonymized SMB retail case study X (email from Solutions Eng).
- Keep pilot small: start with 10 stores, escalate after baseline metrics.

End of dossier — keep this lean, iterate after first call.

-- Aisha
